speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and how long has it been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash itch or cause discomfort for the baby, and do you notice any similar scaling on the diaper area or in skin folds? Also, are there any other family members with eczema, asthma, or hay fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead in a 3-month-old is classic for seborrheic dermatitis, often called cradle cap. I will examine the skin folds to rule out atopic dermatitis and check for any signs of infection. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth (36 weeks), otherwise generally healthy. Family history of psoriasis. Social history: The patient is 3 months old, so the social history is not applicable.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are there any signs of involvement in the diaper area or skin folds, and is the baby showing any signs of discomfort or itching? Also, has the rash spread to other parts of the face or body?

speaker: Patient
text: The patient appears comfortable, with no signs of distress or discomfort noted by the parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you, that helps rule out atopic dermatitis which is usually pruritic. Since the rash is localized to the scalp and forehead with greasy scales and the infant is comfortable, seborrheic dermatitis remains the most likely diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic dermatitis
